title: The Tango Belt and cafes near the district
summary: Leclerc explains the Tango Belt cafes (Anderson's, the Pup Cafe, the Cadillac) lay across Rampart from the district.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What was this business? You know, they have these cabarets. I hear people talk about the Haymarket and the Pup and Toros and Peg Olmsteads. And they talk about the Tango Belt, these things being in the Tango Belt.
Well, the Tango Belt was on the other side of the road, on the other side of the district. That's what they called it. In those days, that's what they called it.

Yeah, it was in the district, all those places across Mason Street, you see. But the cafes like the Anderson's, where Tom Zimmerman played, and the Pup Cafe, and the Cadillac. I played the Cadillac on Ramport and Countdown. I played there for a while. But that was on this side of the road. The other side of the road was supposed to have been the district, you see. That's past Ramport and Basin Street. That's what they called that in those days.
Well, I want to ask you about that since it's a lady present.
